comparison: Both address the core paradoxical finding (C15-C18) that male-female interaction suppresses sleep rebound. OpenEval finds this strongly supported by quantitative data with p<0.001. Peer reviewers also affirmed this as 'very nice' and 'strong,' calling it important enough to merit publication. High agreement on this central finding.

Both evaluate sleep architecture claims (C51, C57, C58). OpenEval finds these supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1, though notes longer monitoring would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting comparison to undisturbed flies and questioning whether changes in bout length/number were properly characterized.

Both address species-specific pheromone effects (C24, C25). OpenEval finds these supported by behavioral scoring data. Peer reviewers also accepted these findings, with Reviewer #1 calling the inter-species data 'very compelling.' Strong agreement on species-specificity evidence.

Both evaluate pheromone removal and post-interaction silencing experiments (C35, C36). OpenEval finds these supported but notes synergy claim is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers marked SUPPORTED, noting these Figure 6 experiments directly addressed earlier concerns about residual pheromones and helped resolve the revision.

Both address female-conditioned tube experiments (C33). OpenEval finds this elegantly demonstrates pheromone sufficiency. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #1 specifically requesting the control of moving males to clean tubes, and Reviewer #3 stating the claim is 'not fully supported.'

Both evaluate thermogenetic activation of pheromone sensing (C34). OpenEval finds strong evidence for sufficiency with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, criticizing the thermogenetic experiments for lacking proper temperature controls and requesting mechanical sleep deprivation followed by pheromone presentation.

Both address P1 neuron activation experiments (C40, C41). OpenEval finds strong evidence that artificial sexual arousal suppresses rebound. Peer reviewers marked SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised, and acceptance in Round 2 indicates these data were convincing.

Both evaluate ppk23 mutant experiments (C32). OpenEval finds strong evidence for necessity of pheromone sensing. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, with significant concerns about data strength, time window selection (ZT0-3 cutting out main effects), and missing controls, calling the ppk-GAL4 experiments 'quite problematic.'

Both address orco mutant experiments ruling out volatile pheromones (C26). OpenEval finds this effectively narrows mechanism to non-volatile signals. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns about the pheromone sensing pathway experiments and statistical validity.

Both evaluate exogenous pheromone experiments (C28). OpenEval finds strong evidence for sufficiency of chemical signals. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, questioning whether effects are due to pheromones versus differential activity, with concerns about experimental design.

Both address memory mutant experiments (C23). OpenEval finds these effectively rule out memory consolidation hypothesis. Peer reviewers accepted these as part of overall narrative without specific critique, treating them as supporting evidence.

Both evaluate TDC2 mutant experiments showing arousal state drives suppression (C46). OpenEval finds elegant evidence but notes complex phenotypes. Peer reviewers marked SUPPORTED with no specific concerns, accepting the logic that when males are aroused by both sexes, both suppress rebound.

Both address TβH mutant experiments on octopamine modulation (C44). OpenEval finds these supported but urges caution due to multiple behavioral effects. Peer reviewers marked SUPPORTED without specific critique of these experiments.

Both evaluate the synergistic model of pheromones and experience (C55, C56). OpenEval notes synergy claim is somewhat speculative without quantitative comparison. Peer reviewers marked SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretive framework after revisions and praising the innovative approach to sleep modulation.

Both address whether rebound is eliminated versus postponed (C50). OpenEval finds this distinction supported but notes longer monitoring would help. Peer reviewers accepted this framework in Round 2, praising the link between sleep homeostasis and sexual arousal.

Both address R2 neuron activity as sleep drive proxy (C20). OpenEval finds this cellular validation strengthens the paradox. Peer reviewers affirmed the core finding without specifically critiquing the R2 neuron data, treating it as part of the strong initial observation.

Both address validation of male-male interaction as sleep deprivation (C14). OpenEval finds this provides important methodological foundation. Peer reviewers affirmed the overall sleep deprivation paradigm as producing a 'strong' initial observation without specific critique of MM validation.

OpenEval evaluated background claims on sleep regulation (C1-C5) as accurately describing well-established prior work with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than standard background.

OpenEval evaluated background claims on environmental sleep modulation (C6-C9) as accurately summarizing prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual background claims.

OpenEval evaluated discussion claims citing precedent for modulation of sleep homeostasis (C47-C49) as accurately citing prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion/context claims.

OpenEval evaluated claim that pheromone sensing modulates rather than triggers courtship (C52), finding it supported by citations and unpublished observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic clarification.

OpenEval evaluated claims positioning work relative to concurrent studies (C53-C54) as accurately citing relevant prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature positioning claims.
